To evaluate the determinant of the matrix 
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
1 & x & y \\ 
1 & x + y & y \\ 
1 & x & x + y 
\end{vmatrix},
\]
we will use cofactor expansion along the first row. The determinant is given by:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
1 & x & y \\ 
1 & x + y & y \\ 
1 & x & x + y 
\end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} x + y & y \\ x & x + y \end{vmatrix} - x \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & y \\ 1 & x + y \end{vmatrix} + y \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x + y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix}.
\]

First, we compute each of the 2x2 determinants. The first one is:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} x + y & y \\ x & x + y \end{vmatrix} = (x + y)(x + y) - (y)(x) = x^2 + 2xy + y^2 - yx = x^2 + xy + y^2.
\]

The second one is:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 1 & y \\ 1 & x + y \end{vmatrix} = (1)(x + y) - (1)(y) = x + y - y = x.
\]

The third one is:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x + y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix} = (1)(x) - (1)(x + y) = x - x - y = -y.
\]

Substituting these back into the original expression, we get:
\[
1 \cdot (x^2 + xy + y^2) - x \cdot x + y \cdot (-y) = x^2 + xy + y^2 - x^2 - y^2 = xy.
\]

Thus, the determinant of the matrix is:
\[
\boxed{xy}.
\]

Substituting these back into the cofactor expansion, we get:
\[

\]

\[

\]

\]

3. \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x + y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix}\):
\[

\]

Substitute these results back into the determinant formula:

\[
\text{det}(A) = 1 \cdot (x^2 + xy + y^2) - x \cdot x + y \cdot (-y)
\]

Simplify the expression:

\[
\text{det}(A) = x^2 + xy + y^2 - x^2 - y^2
\]

Combine like terms:

\[
\text{det}(A) = x^2 - x^2 + xy + y^2 - y^2 = xy
\]

Thus, the determinant of the matrix is:

\boxed{xy}
